title: Business Breakfast | Stock/Share Market News | 29th July 2026 | TV5 Money

recommendations.note: Keep holding - it is improving right now and his buy price will definitely come back easily.
recommendations.detail: Caller Ganesh said his portfolio is 75% in profit overall but three stocks are in a loss, and asked whether to average or exit. On Nuvoco Vistas, Kutumba Rao said he would say keep holding it, because it is improving right now and the caller's price will definitely come back, easily.
The same caller is in a loss on Spandana Sphoorty. Kutumba Rao's verdict was blunt: as for Spandana, he would say sell on rallies, clearly. No averaging.
The third loss-making stock in the same caller's portfolio was NCC. Kutumba Rao said the second stock, NCC, he would also say hold, as of now.

recommendations.price: exit on a small rally up to 250-260
recommendations.note: June result only seasonally decent and the stock is near its 52-week low - exit on a rally to 250-260.
recommendations.detail: A caller asked what to do with Rallis India. Kutumba Rao said it is one of the biggest stocks in the Tata Group, and in June they showed a somewhat decent result as usual, but even year on year he would not call it a great result because it is a seasonal result - which is why the stock is near its 52-week low. So in Rallis, maybe if a small rally comes up to 250, 260, when it comes like that he would say exit.

recommendations.note: A stock to watch - consolidating strongly and can slowly emerge as one of the bigger NBFCs.
recommendations.detail: Reviewing the results the anchor had run through, Kutumba Rao singled one out: he would say Tata Capital is a stock to watch. It is consolidating strongly, and maybe it can slowly emerge as one of the bigger NBFCs - one can expect that of Tata Capital - so he said to observe it carefully. (Its result showed profit after tax up 56%.)

recommendations.note: The one aggressive rollover; now the flagship liquor stock, and liquor may outperform in the medium term.
recommendations.detail: In his F&O read, Kutumba Rao said speculative longs were not worth considering because yesterday was rollover day, but if one stock showed a somewhat aggressive rollover he would say it is Radico. Radico has now become the flagship company for the claim that liquor companies are performing well, so he definitely said to observe it, and added that liquor stocks may perhaps also be outperformers in the medium term.

recommendations.note: Extremely good Q1 and order inflow; may not jump immediately but a slow rise from here is clearly visible.
recommendations.detail: On the infra space, Kutumba Rao called L&T's result extremely good, because the order inflow also increased - they now have a project pipeline of nearly Rs 15 lakh crore and Q1 rose more than 14%, which he said is extremely good for infra companies. If order books keep growing and government infrastructure spending increases, the infra stocks that have underperformed until now will perform better. It may not jump immediately - even L&T may not jump immediately - but slowly, from here, the possibility of it definitely rising is clearly visible.

recommendations.note: Hold for now - the NSE IPO is ahead, though brokers' incomes may have dipped this quarter after the bank-guarantee change.
recommendations.detail: A mailer holding BSE shares bought at Rs 3,300 asked what to do as the stock keeps falling. Kutumba Rao said as of now he would say hold, because the NSE IPO is also ahead. He added that, as he had said in the opening remarks, after the bank-guarantee issue and the related changes there are doubts as to whether brokers' incomes have fallen a bit in this quarter, and the market discounts that in advance - but for now, hold.

recommendations.note: Agreed the result disappointed on profitability, but said don't compare the March year-ending quarter - year on year it is okay.
recommendations.detail: Niranjan holds 6,000 shares of Suzlon at Rs 60 and the anchor called the result disappointing. Kutumba Rao agreed he too would call it a disappointment, because this is a consolidation and turnaround counter: for the last four quarters the top line has been growing without losses, but profitability has not been improving, maybe because raw-material and metal costs played a big part, and their top line has fallen a lot. When the anchor pointed to the quarter-on-quarter drop from Rs 5,500 crore to Rs 3,800 crore, Kutumba Rao corrected him - that is the year-ending quarter, when government orders are higher, so the March quarter should never be used for comparison; year on year, he said, it is okay.
